prompt: Deliver the safety briefing before the annual Thanksgiving backyard football game. It must address the specific documented dangers of at least three named uncles, and be worded cautiously enough that Aunt Denise, a paralegal, cannot object to any sentence.
response:
Ladies, gentlemen, and especially players, if I could have your attention for a moment before the coin toss.

Thank you. This briefing is intended to promote a safe environment for today’s annual Thanksgiving game. I will now review a few reminders tailored to conditions we have observed in prior years.

First, all participants are reminded that the section of the lawn nearest the birdbath has been documented to retain moisture significantly longer than the surrounding turf. The traction hazard in this zone is foreseeable. All players are advised to reduce their speed when entering that quadrant. This advisory applies generally, though the record indicates that Uncle Mike, in particular, has historically accelerated through that zone. The family respectfully requests that this pattern not be repeated.

Second, the rules of touch football will be interpreted today as requiring contact that is both incidental and minimal. The league wishes to expressly prohibit any technique involving a lowered shoulder, a stiff arm delivered above the sternum, or what has previously been described, in Uncle Ron’s own post-game commentary, as a “veteran move.” A veteran move of any kind is not recognized in our bylaws and should be considered outside the scope of play.

Third, regarding the defensive formation near the Weber grill: the grill’s metal housing retains ambient heat from its most recent use. Physical contact with the grill during a play could result in a thermal injury. Players are asked to maintain a buffer distance of no less than two full arm’s lengths. For clarity, this guidance is intended for all participants, and specifically serves as notice that the maneuver colloquially attributed to Uncle Steve—cornering a receiver against the grill’s closed lid—constitutes an avoidable hazard and must not occur.

Finally, for the benefit of all bystanders, including those observing from the deck, any interpretation of these guidelines should favor the safety of the participants over the competitive outcome of the game. By taking the field, each player acknowledges these reminders and accepts that the sole objective is a recreational contest conducted in a spirit of mutual care.

Thank you, and please enjoy the game.
